questions.question: Users can SSH into the compute instances which make up a Virtual Warehouse. True or false?

explanation.correct: Users have no access to the underlying resources of a virtual warehouse.

questions.question: What attributes make Snowflake a SaaS solution? Choose two correct values.

options.text: Pay for what you use pricing plan.
The ability to SSH into underlying compute instances.
Snowflake can be installed on a local machine.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, C: No hardware to manage.; Pay for what you use pricing plan..

questions.question: Which cloud platforms can a Snowflake account be hosted in? Choose three correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, C, E: Amazon Web Services (AWS); Microsoft Azure; Google Cloud Platform.

questions.question: Which layers are in Snowflake’s Multi-cluster Shared Data Architecture? Choose two correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, C: Storage Layer; Compute / Query Processing Layer.

questions.question: Snowflake partitions files loaded into Snowflake automatically. True or false?

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: True.

questions.question: What is the process of eliminating unrequired micro-partitions called during a query? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: This is the process of ignoring micro-partitions which aren't required to fulfil a user query.

questions.question: Databases are not required to have a unique identifier. True or false?

explanation.correct: Database objects are required to have a unique identifier within an account.

questions.question: Which layer of the Multi-cluster Shared Data Architecture handles user authentication? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is D: Services..

questions.question: Which of the following values are Snowflake editions? Choose two correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, D: Standard; Enterprise.

questions.question: Which statement is incorrect regarding snowflake editions? Choose one correct value.

options.text: The Standard edition has the Time Travel feature.
The Enterprise edition contains all the features of the Standard edition.
The Business Critical edition has additional support for regulation compliance around data protection.
The Enterprise edition contains all the features of the Business Critical edition.

explanation.correct: In reality this statement is reversed. The Business Critical edition contains all the features of the Enterprise edition.

questions.question: What is the definition of Tri-secret secure? Choose one correct value.

options.text: The use of three passwords to log-in.
A composite encryption key to encrypt data files made up a user provider key and a Snowflake key.
The use of a hardware module to store a customer managed key.

explanation.correct: More information - https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/security-encryption-manage.html#tri-secret-secure

questions.question: All objects are individually securable. True or false?

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: True.

questions.question: Which objects are schema-level objects? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, D, F: Table.; Stream.; Stored Procedure..

questions.question: How many geographic regions in a cloud platform can a Snowflake account be deployed into? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Each account is provisioned in a single geographic region.

questions.question: What is the section in bold of the following Snowflake account URL referred to as: xy12345.us-east-2.aws.snowflakecomputing.com? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The account locator, account region and account cloud platform taken together are referred to as the account identifier.

questions.question: A schema cannot be cloned. True or false?

explanation.correct: A clone can be created with the following command: CREATE SCHEMA <SCHEMA_CLONE> CLONE <SCHEMA>;

questions.question: Which table type does have the fail-safe feature? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: Permanent.

questions.question: Of the following options which is the most accurate definition of a materialized view? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Stores results of a query definition and periodically refreshes its data.
Does not store data only a query definition.
The underlying query definition is only visible to authorized users.
A query is executed once and the results are stored for later user and are not refreshed in the future.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: Stores results of a query definition and periodically refreshes its data..

questions.question: Which type of view bypasses some query optimizations to improve data security? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: This may result is poorer query performance than a standard view but makes the view more secure.

questions.question: Time Travel is not possible on transient tables. True or false?

explanation.correct: Regardless of the Snowflake edition, transient tables can only set a Time Travel retention period of up to 1 day.

questions.question: Fail-safe is available for external tables. True or false?

explanation.correct: It is only available for permanent table types.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of Time Travel days for a table of the permanent type? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: This is true for permanent tables on the Enterprise edition or higher. For the standard edition of Snowflake the maximum number of Time Travel days (also called retention period) is 1 day.

questions.question: Which languages can be used with a User Defined Function (UDF)? Choose four correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, B, E, G: SQL; Python; Java; JavaScript.

questions.question: User Defined Functions can't be called as part of a SQL statement. True or false?

explanation.correct: This command shows the use of a UDF as part of a SQL statement: SELECT AREA_OF_CIRCLE(col1) FROM MY_TABLE;

questions.question: What does it mean to overload a User Defined Function (UDF)? Choose one correct value.

options.text: The ability to call a UDF from within another UDF.
The ability of a UDF to accept more than one argument.
A UDF can returning more than one row.
The ability for multiple UDFs to exist with the same identifier but different input arguments.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is D: The ability for multiple UDFs to exist with the same identifier but different input arguments..

questions.question: Which object does an external function make use of to hold security related information? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: An API integration object stores information about an HTTPS proxy service, including information about: The cloud platform provider The type of proxy service The identifier and access credentials for a cloud platform role that has sufficient privileges to use the proxy service.

questions.question: Virtual warehouses are billed on a per second basis. What is the minimum number of seconds a virtual warehouse is billed for? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Snowflake credits are calculated with a minimum of 60 seconds.

questions.question: Data storage is calculated based on the on-disk bytes in the which of the following locations? Choose two correct values.

options.text: Database tables including time travel & fail-safe.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, D: Database tables including time travel & fail-safe.; Internal stages..

questions.question: What is the SnowSQL CLI tool used for? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Diagnosing network connectivity to Snowflake from client tools.
Connecting to and issuing SQL commands to Snowflake via the command line.
Troubleshoot data corruption issues in storage layer.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B: Connecting to and issuing SQL commands to Snowflake via the command line..

questions.question: You can execute commands as the ACCOUNTADMIN using the SnowSQL CLI tool. True or False?

explanation.correct: You can execute commands using the SnowSQL CLI tool with any role you have the privileges to assume.

questions.question: Which is the most accurate description of the Snowflake Partner Connect? Choose one correct value.

options.text: The Snowflake Partner Connect allows you to easily create trial account with selected Snowflake business partners and integrate these accounts with Snowflake.
The Snowflake Partner Connect allows an account to securely import data from a business partners Snowflake account.
The Snowflake Partner Connect allows Snowflake data to be exported to a business partners Snowflake account.
The Snowflake Partner Connect exposes contact details for third-party data providers, so a user can connect with them in their own time.

explanation.correct: The Snowflake Partner Connect is a service which expedites the process of getting up and running with selected third-party tools.

questions.question: How many days is the query history maintained in the history tab of the classic UI? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is D: 14.

questions.question: On which version of Snowflake is Secure Data Sharing not available? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Due to the stricter security requirements and isolated environment the account exists in, VPS does not support secure data sharing.

questions.question: What do you configure a SHARE object with? Choose two correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C, D: Object privileges.; Account identifiers..

questions.question: How many databases can a data provider add to a SHARE object? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Only one database can be added per share.

questions.question: Data providers can share data with a data consumer in a different cloud region or cloud provider. True or false?

explanation.correct: Replication to an account in the data consumer’s region is a prerequisite.

questions.question: How many accounts can a data consumer share a shared database with? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Data consumers cannot re-share shared database objects.

questions.question: Which sentence most accurately describes what a Virtual Warehouse is? Choose one correct value.

options.text: A Virtual Warehouse is another name for the persistent storage layer.
A Virtual warehouse is a named abstraction for one or more compute nodes.
A virtual warehouse is a way of logically grouping schemas.
A virtual warehouse is a cluster of compute nodes the user sets up and maintains.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B: A Virtual warehouse is a named abstraction for one or more compute nodes..

questions.question: The following command is permitted when interacting with a Virtual Warehouse: ALTER WAREHOUSE DE_VW SET WAREHOUSE_SIZE=LARGE. True or false?

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: True.

questions.question: What is the query to remove a virtual warehouse? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: DROP WAREHOUSE MY_WAREHOUSE;.

questions.question: How would a user choose the size of a virtual warehouse? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Always use x-small as it’s the cheapest.
Create multiple x-small clusters and if queueing occurs direct users to a different x-small virtual warehouse.
Experimenting with a representative query of a workload on a variety of virtual warehouse sizes to find the correct fit that matches desired run-times.
Experimenting with a representative query of a workload on the largest virtual warehouse size and monitor its performance in order to assess if it matches desired run-times.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: Experimenting with a representative query of a workload on a variety of virtual warehouse sizes to find the correct fit that matches desired run-times..

questions.question: Data loading typically requires the use of a XXL Virtual Warehouse. True or false?

explanation.correct: Data loading does not typically require large Virtual Warehouses and sizing up does not guarantee increased data loading performance.

questions.question: In which state is a Virtual Warehouse billable? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: When a Virtual Warehouse is in the ‘STARTED’ state it will accrue Snowflake credits regardless of whether queries are being executed using it or not.

questions.question: What is the function of the AUTO_SUSPEND property of a Virtual Warehouse? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Specifies if a Virtual Warehouse should be suspended immediately after its created.
Specifies whether to automatically resume a warehouse when a SQL statement is submitted to it.
Specifies the number of seconds of inactivity after which a warehouse is automatically suspended.
Specifies the max threshold of queries after which point a virtual warehouse will be automatically suspended.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: Specifies the number of seconds of inactivity after which a warehouse is automatically suspended..

questions.question: What is the function of the INITIALLY_SUSPENDED property of a Virtual Warehouse? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Specifies if a Virtual Warehouse should be suspended immediately after its created.
Specifies whether to automatically resume a warehouse when a SQL statement is submitted to it.
Specifies the number of seconds of inactivity after which a warehouse is automatically suspended.
Specifies the max threshold of queries after which point a virtual warehouse will be automatically suspended.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: Specifies if a Virtual Warehouse should be suspended immediately after its created..

questions.question: A data engineer is running some transformation jobs using a M virtual warehouse. The virtual warehouse seems to be suspending between the jobs, making subsequent jobs take longer. What could be the issue? Choose one correct value.

options.text: The Virtual Warehouse AUTO_RESUME property is set to FALSE.
The Virtual Warehouse INITIALLY_SUSPEND property is set to TRUE.
The Virtual Warehouse is too small for the workload they're running.
The Virtual Warehouse AUTO_SUSPEND property (in seconds) is set too low.

explanation.correct: If the AUTO_SUSPEND property is set too low this can cause the virtual warehouse to go into the suspended state quicker than is desired. This can cause subsequent jobs to run slower because virtual warehouse will purge their cache when suspended.

questions.question: Which configuration of min_cluster_count & max_cluster_count would put a muti-cluster warehouse in maximized mode? Choose two correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, C: MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT=1 & MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT=1; MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT=4 & MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT=4.

questions.question: What are the two scaling policies that can be defined when creating a multi-cluster warehouse? Choose two correct values.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, C: Standard; Economy.

questions.question: Why would a materialized view be used? Select all that apply.

options.text: Materialized views are cheaper than storing data in a table.
Materialized views can be created on top of external tables to improve their query performance.
Materialized views make complex queries that are commonly executed readily available.
Materialized views store data temporarily during the data loading process.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, C: Materialized views can be created on top of external tables to improve their query performance.; Materialized views make complex queries that are commonly executed readily available..

questions.question: Materialized views contribute to both compute and storage costs. True or false?

explanation.correct: Compute: background maintenance is performed on Materialized views to keep them up to date with their base table. Storage: each materialized view stores its query result, adding to the monthly storage usage for an account.

questions.question: Natural clustering is determined by the order in which data is loaded. True or false?

explanation.correct: Table data is partitioned and stored in the order it was loaded.

questions.question: Which system function is called to retrieve clustering metadata for a column or columns? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B: system$clustering_information.

questions.question: Automatic clustering improves performance on queries that include which of the following constructs? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: Clustering improves performance of queries that frequently filter or sort on the clustered keys.

questions.question: What is the recommended maximum number of columns (or expressions) defined per clustering key? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is D: 2.

questions.question: Which queries are examples of selective point lookups? Select all that apply.

options.text: SELECT NAME, ADDRESS FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE EMP_EMAIL = ‘support.help@corp.com’;
SELECT NAME, ADDRESS, COUNT(FLAG) FROM EMPLOYEES GROUP BY NAME, ADDRESS;
SELECT NAME, ADDRESS FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE EMP_ID IN (‘12867’,’0987SS’);

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, D: SELECT NAME, ADDRESS FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE EMP_EMAIL = ‘support.help@corp.com’;; SELECT NAME, ADDRESS FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE EMP_ID IN (‘12867’,’0987SS’);.

questions.question: Which queries would not require the use of a Virtual Warehouse and instead would make use of the metadata cache? Select all that apply.

options.text: SELECT EMP_ID, NAME, ADDRESS FROM EMPLOYEE;

explanation.correct: The number of rows along with a description of tables is maintained in the metadata cache and so doesn't need a Virtual Warehouse to compute the result.

questions.question: To reuse the results cache which of the following requirements must be met? Select all that apply.

options.text: The same role is used as in the previous query.
The same user is used as in the previous query.
The underlying table data has changed since the previous query.
The new query exactly matches the previous query.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, D: The same role is used as in the previous query.; The new query exactly matches the previous query..

questions.question: The following query can make use of the results cache: SELECT NAME, EMP_ID, CURRENT_TIME() FROM EMPLOYEE. True of false?

explanation.correct: If time context functions are used, such as CURRENT_TIME(), the result cache will not be used.

questions.question: If the query profile indicates queries are regularly spilling to remote storage what are the recommended solutions? Select all that apply.

options.text: Decrease the size of the Virtual Warehouse.
Increase the size of the Virtual Warehouse.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, D: Increase the size of the Virtual Warehouse.; Process data in smaller batches..

questions.question: What level of cardinality is it recommended a column have when selected in a query that makes use of a GROUP BY? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Having many distinct values can be a very memory-intensive operation, a lot of data will be spilled to disk and there will be high network usage.

questions.question: Which symbols are used when referencing a user stage via SQL? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: @~.

questions.question: Which symbols are used when referencing a table stage via SQL? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B: @%.

questions.question: When is a table stage not appropriate to use for data loading? Select all that apply.

options.text: When a single user wants to load data into a single table.
When multiple users want to load data into multiple tables.
When a single user wants to load data into multiple tables.
When multiple users want to load data into a single table.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B, C: When multiple users want to load data into multiple tables.; When a single user wants to load data into multiple tables..

questions.question: If the PURGE copy option were set to TRUE what would happen to data files that are successfully loaded into Snowflake from an external stage? Choose one correct value.

options.text: They would be transferred to a different cloud storage bucket.
They would be removed from Snowflake long-term table storage.
They would be removed from the external stage.
They would be removed from the external stage and Snowflake long-term table storage.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: They would be removed from the external stage..

questions.question: Which INSERT query would return an error? Choose one correct value.

options.text: INSERT INTO TABLE EMPLOYEE SELECT ‘001’, ‘Irene Adler’, ‘10/10/1976’;
INSERT INTO TABLE MY_TABLE (ID, NAME) SELECT ‘001’, ‘Irene Adler’;
INSERT INTO TABLE MY_TABLE (ID, NAME) SELECT ‘001’, ‘Irene Adler’, ‘10/10/1976’;
INSERT INTO TABLE MY_TABLE SELECT * FROM MY_TABLE_2;

explanation.correct: If specifying the columns in an INSERT statement you cannot include additional data in the select query.

questions.question: The COPY INTO <table> statement does NOT require a virtual warehouse to run. True or false?

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B: False.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the TYPE option when creating a file format object? Choose one correct value.

options.text: If the file format object will be used with views or tables.
If the file format object will be permanent or temporary.
Specifies the type of file the file format object will be configured to parse.
Specifies the type of compression the file format will use to uncompress files.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: Specifies the type of file the file format object will be configured to parse..

questions.question: Which properties are not available to a file format object of type CSV? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: These properties are available if the type property of a file format object is set to JSON.

questions.question: What is the recommended compressed file size when loading data into Snowflake? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is D: 100-250mb.

questions.question: When copying files from a table to an internal stage using the COPY INTO <location> command, the results are split into multiple files. Which copy option would I use to ensure only one file is produced? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: SINGLE accepts a boolean that specifies whether to generate a single file or multiple files.

questions.question: Which semi-structured data formats do Snowflake can natively store and query? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, C, D, E, H, I: JSON; CSV; AVRO; PARQUET; ORC; XML.

questions.question: Which function can be used to automatically detect a schema definition? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: A sample command making use of the INFER_SCHEMA function: CREATE TABLE SS_TABLE USING TEMPLATE ( SELECT ARRAY_AGG(OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(*)) FROM TABLE( INFER_SCHEMA( LOCATION=>'@MYSTAGE', FILE_FORMAT=>'FF_PARQUET' )));

questions.question: Which query would result in an error when parsing a column of type VARIANT given the following JSON: { “employee” : { “name” : “Jason Rojas”, “_id” : “UNX789544” }, “joined_on” : “10-09-2019”, “skills” : [“Java”, “Kotlin”, “Android”] } Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Column names are case insensitive but elements are case sensitive, so referring to the element 'name' with a capital N would result in an error.

questions.question: Which types of notation are used to traverse semi-structured data natively in Snowflake? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, B: Dot notation.; Bracket notation..

questions.question: Snowflake uses the following access control schemes: role based access control (RBAC) and _________. Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: Discretionary Access Control (DAC).

questions.question: Every securable object is owned by a single role. True or false?

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: True.

questions.question: The ACCOUNTADMIN can perform the same functions as the SECURITYADMIN, SYSADMIN & ORGAMIN. True or false?

explanation.correct: ORGADMIN is for managing operation at an organization level and is not possible with the ACCOUNTADMIN role.

questions.question: Which system-defined role is it recommended to assign custom roles to? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: If custom roles are not assigned to the SYSADMIN role, system admins will not be able to manage the objects owned by the custom role.

questions.question: Network policies currently support which type of IP address? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A: IPv4.

questions.question: If enabled, periodic rekeying happens every ___ months. Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: "If periodic rekeying is enabled, then when the retired encryption key for a table is older than one year, Snowflake automatically creates a new encryption key and re-encrypts all data previously protected by the retired key using the new key. The new key is used to decrypt the table data going forward." - https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/security-encryption-manage.html#periodic-rekeying

questions.question: What is the function of a row access policy? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Restricting users from inserting rows into certain tables.
Restricting which rows are returned in a query.
Giving access to table data to non-snowflake users.
Giving read access to a table to non-ownership roles.

explanation.correct: Row access policies enable a security team to restrict which rows are return in a query.

questions.question: The account usage share contains a database called SNOWFLAKE. The views in this database are used to provide fine-grained metrics at the account and object level. What is the maximum number of months data in these views available for? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Certain account usage views provide historical usage metrics. The retention period for these views is 1 year.

questions.question: What does each database created in an account automatically include? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Each database created in an account automatically includes a built-in, read-only schema named INFORMATION_SCHEMA based on the SQL-92 ANSI Information Schema.

questions.question: Snowflake provides a suite of powerful features that ensure the highest possible levels of data security. Which statements are correct regarding Snowflake? Select all that apply.

options.text: Snowflake makes use of key-pair authentication for programmatic access.
Snowflake uses a hierarchical key model which is rooted in a hardware key.
Tri-secret secure makes use of a composite key made up of a customer managed key and a Snowflake managed key.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, B, C, D: Snowflake support discretionary access control. (DAC); Snowflake makes use of key-pair authentication for programmatic access.; Snowflake uses a hierarchical key model which is rooted in a hardware key.; Tri-secret secure makes use of a composite key made up of a customer managed key and a Snowflake managed key..

questions.question: Micro-partitions can be modified once they have been created. True or false?

explanation.correct: Micro-partitions are immutable.

questions.question: What is the default compression format used when unloading files from Snowflake using the GET command? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: GZIP.

questions.question: What is the default value for the table property DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS for an account on the enterprise edition of Snowflake? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The default value for DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS is 1 for all editions of Snowflake.

questions.question: What’s the maximum number of days a user could set the table property DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS to for a transient table on a business critical edition Snowflake account? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: The maximum DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS is 0 or 1 for temporary and transient tables regardless of the edition of Snowflake.

questions.question: There is a configuration property for tables to disable Time Travel. True or false?

explanation.correct: However, DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS can be set to 0 on the account level or object level to effectively disable time travel.

questions.question: Which SQL extensions did Snowflake add for use with the Time Travel feature? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, C, E: AT; BEFORE; UNDROP.

questions.question: Cloning a table copies the underlying data effectively doubling storage costs. True or false?

explanation.correct: Cloning does not contribute to storage costs until data is modified or new data is added to the clone.

questions.question: A Snowflake user creates a clone of a 'TABLE_A' and names it 'TABLE_B'. When new records are inserted into 'TABLE A' what is expected to happen to 'TABLE B'? Choose one correct value.

options.text: The inserted records show immediately in TABLE B.
The inserted records show after a short delay in TABLE B.
The inserted records do not show at all in TABLE B.
The inserted records do not show at all in TABLE B until TABLE A is dropped.

explanation.correct: Changes made to the source or the clone are not reflected between each other, they are completely independent.

questions.question: External stages can be cloned. True or false?

explanation.correct: External tables and internal named stages are never cloned.

questions.question: Which Snowflake object would be ideal to schedule an execution to refresh a secondary database for replication? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: A task object can execute a single SQL statement.

questions.question: Which result from the APPROXIMATE_SIMILARITY estimation function would indicate two sets of rows overlap significantly but are not identical? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: 0 indicates no overlap and 1 indicates the two sets are identical. 0.8 would indicate two sets are very similar.

questions.question: As a data engineer I want to create a file URL that is only valid for 24hours. Which file function would I use? Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Outputs an encoded URL granting access to a file for 24 hours to the user that requested it.

questions.question: What is the behavior of the COPY INTO <table> command when the ON_ERROR option is set to CONTINUTE? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Skip file when error is found.
Load the file if errors are found.
Skip a file when a certain number of errors is found.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is B: Load the file if errors are found..

questions.question: What is the purpose of the VALIDATE function? Choose one correct value.

options.text: Allows a user to perform a dry-run of the load process to expose errors.
Outputs a pdf to a configured stage of all the errors of a past execution.
Allows a user to view all errors encountered during a previous COPY INTO execution.
Allows a user to view all errors encountered during all previous runs of a COPY INTO execution.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is C: Allows a user to view all errors encountered during a previous COPY INTO execution..

questions.question: Which SQL commands would show the contents of a stage? Select all that apply.

explanation.correct: The correct answer is A, D: LIST @MY_STAGE;; ls @MY_STAGE;.

questions.question: Filters should be used as _________ as possible. Choose one correct value.

explanation.correct: Use filters such as a WHERE clause as early as possible to improve pruning for subsequent processing steps such as a GROUP BY.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake worksheets is true?

options.text: Worksheets are where SQL commands are executed in Snowflake.
A worksheet can only be accessed by the user who created it.
Worksheets do not allow sharing SQL queries with other users.
Worksheets are automatically named based on the user role.

explanation.correct: Worksheets in Snowflake are used to execute SQL commands and manage queries.

whyOthersWrong.b: Worksheets can be shared with other users within the organization, provided the appropriate permissions are granted.
whyOthersWrong.c: Worksheets can be shared, and users can grant permissions to others to access and view the content.
whyOthersWrong.d: Worksheets are named based on timestamps when created but can be renamed manually for clarity.

questions.question: What is the function of a compute warehouse in Snowflake when executing a query?

options.text: It stores the results of the queries.
It provides the compute power required to execute queries.
It manages user permissions and security roles.
It is only used for managing storage resources.

explanation.correct: The compute warehouse in Snowflake is responsible for providing the necessary compute resources to run queries and process data.

whyOthersWrong.a: The compute warehouse is not responsible for storing query results; storage is managed separately.
whyOthersWrong.c: User permissions and security roles are managed separately from the compute warehouse.
whyOthersWrong.d: The compute warehouse focuses on compute power rather than managing storage, which is handled by Snowflake’s storage layer.

questions.question: What components make up a fully qualified table name in Snowflake? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: The table name is part of the fully qualified name used in SQL queries. The schema name is included as part of the structure that organizes tables within databases. The database name is also part of the fully qualified table name, specifying the location of the schema and table.

whyOthersWrong.d: The compute warehouse name is not part of the fully qualified table name; it refers to the compute resources used to run queries.

questions.question: What is the role of the "Query History" section in the Snowflake interface?

options.text: It allows users to review and manage past queries executed in Snowflake.
It provides a list of all databases and schemas available in the Snowflake account.
It enables users to rename worksheets and change their roles.
It stores the logs of all SQL errors encountered by Snowflake.

explanation.correct: The "Query History" section in Snowflake allows users to review past queries they have executed, view their status, and access execution details for performance analysis.

whyOthersWrong.b: The list of databases and schemas is available in the "Data" section, not in the "Query History" section.
whyOthersWrong.c: Renaming worksheets and managing roles are done in the worksheets section, not in "Query History."
whyOthersWrong.d: While the "Query History" may show errors for specific queries, it does not exclusively store error logs; it provides an overview of all queries executed.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Snowflake's architecture?

explanation.correct: This is correct. Snowflake uses a "Multi-cluster shared data architecture," which combines elements of both the shared disk and shared nothing architectures to optimize scalability, performance, and data management.

whyOthersWrong.a: While Snowflake uses clusters, it does not follow the traditional "shared nothing" model entirely; it incorporates a central storage repository similar to shared disk systems.
whyOthersWrong.b: Snowflake incorporates elements of shared disk architecture but is not limited to this approach; it combines multiple clusters with shared data storage.
whyOthersWrong.d: Snowflake's architecture is not limited to a single node; it supports scaling with multiple clusters.

questions.question: What are the three distinct independent layers in Snowflake's architecture? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: The Cloud Services Layer, also referred to as the brain of the system, manages authentication, query parsing, and optimization. The Compute Layer (also known as the query processing layer) is responsible for executing queries using virtual warehouses. The Storage Layer manages Snowflake’s data storage, using hybrid columnar storage techniques.

whyOthersWrong.c: Metadata management is part of the Cloud Services Layer, not an independent layer.

questions.question: In Snowflake, where does query execution take place?

explanation.correct: Query execution in Snowflake occurs in the Compute Layer, also known as the query processing layer, which uses virtual warehouses for compute resources.

whyOthersWrong.a: The Cloud Services Layer is responsible for query parsing and optimization, not execution.
whyOthersWrong.b: The Storage Layer stores data, but the actual execution of queries happens in the Compute Layer.
whyOthersWrong.d: There is no separate "Authentication Layer" in Snowflake; authentication is managed within the Cloud Services Layer.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Cloud Services Layer in Snowflake?

options.text: Storing data in a hybrid columnar format
Providing compute resources for query execution
Managing authentication, access control, and query optimization
Storing logs of all user activity

explanation.correct: The Cloud Services Layer in Snowflake manages critical functions such as authentication, access control, metadata management, query parsing, and query optimization.

whyOthersWrong.a: Storing data is the role of the Storage Layer, not the Cloud Services Layer.
whyOthersWrong.b: Compute resources for query execution are provided by the Compute Layer, not the Cloud Services Layer.
whyOthersWrong.d: While the Cloud Services Layer manages metadata, it does not specifically store logs of all user activity; logs are part of the broader monitoring and logging features within Snowflake.

questions.question: What is one advantage of the shared disk architecture that Snowflake integrates into its multi-cluster shared data architecture?

options.text: Centralized data storage for simplified management

explanation.correct: The shared disk architecture provides a central data repository, which simplifies data management. Snowflake incorporates this concept into its architecture for efficient storage access and simplified management.

whyOthersWrong.a: The shared disk model simplifies data management, not complicates it.
whyOthersWrong.b: Although a single point of failure is a disadvantage of shared disk architecture, it is not an advantage that Snowflake incorporates.
whyOthersWrong.d: The shared disk architecture can face bottlenecks when scaling due to all nodes needing to communicate with the central storage, so this is not the advantage Snowflake adopts.

questions.question: Which of the following Snowflake editions is designed to meet the needs of large-scale enterprises and includes features like multi-cluster warehouses?

explanation.correct: The Enterprise Edition includes all features from the Standard Edition plus additional capabilities like multi-cluster warehouses, which are essential for large-scale enterprises requiring efficient scalability.

whyOthersWrong.a: This edition is suitable for foundational use but does not include enterprise-specific features like multi-cluster warehouses.
whyOthersWrong.c: This edition is for companies needing additional security features beyond what Enterprise offers.
whyOthersWrong.d: This edition provides the highest security level with dedicated servers, exceeding standard enterprise needs.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition provides dedicated servers and a separate environment for companies dealing with highly sensitive data?

explanation.correct: This is the basic edition and does not offer such high-level security features.

whyOthersWrong.b: Although it offers more advanced features than Standard, it does not provide dedicated servers.
whyOthersWrong.c: While it includes enhanced security features, it still does not provide the fully isolated environment and dedicated hardware like the Virtual Private Edition.
whyOthersWrong.d: The Virtual Private Edition offers the highest level of security, including dedicated servers and a completely isolated environment, which is necessary for organizations dealing with highly sensitive data.

questions.question: What is the maximum duration for Time Travel in the Enterprise Edition of Snowflake?

explanation.correct: In the Enterprise Edition, Time Travel is extended to a maximum of 90 days, allowing users to query historical data for a longer period than the Standard Edition.

whyOthersWrong.a: This is the limit for Time Travel in the Standard Edition, not Enterprise.
whyOthersWrong.b: This duration is related to Snowflake's Fail-safe feature, not Time Travel.
whyOthersWrong.c: There is no 30-day limit for Time Travel in any Snowflake edition; Enterprise offers up to 90 days.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature available in the Business Critical Edition but not in the Enterprise Edition?

explanation.correct: The Business Critical Edition includes advanced security features such as customer-managed encryption, which is not available in the Enterprise Edition.

whyOthersWrong.a: This feature is available starting from the Enterprise Edition.
whyOthersWrong.b: This is also available in the Enterprise Edition.
whyOthersWrong.d: Column-level security is part of the Enterprise Edition, not exclusive to Business Critical.

questions.question: True or False: The Standard Edition of Snowflake includes disaster recovery features called Fail-safe for up to 7 days beyond Time Travel.

explanation.correct: The Fail-safe feature, which allows disaster recovery for up to 7 days beyond the Time Travel period, is available in all Snowflake editions, including the Standard Edition.

whyOthersWrong.b: This is incorrect because Fail-safe is indeed a feature available in all editions of Snowflake, including the Standard Edition.

questions.question: Which of the following commands provides general statistics about table storage in Snowflake?

explanation.correct: This command gives general information about table storage, including table properties like clustering and optimization. It’s suitable for quick overviews.

whyOthersWrong.a: This would be valid if querying a view, but it’s not a command. The TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS views in the information and account usage schemas provide more detailed storage information.
whyOthersWrong.c: This is not a valid command in Snowflake for retrieving storage information.
whyOthersWrong.d: This is not a valid command in Snowflake; it does not exist.

questions.question: What is the role required to query the TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS view from the account usage schema in Snowflake?

explanation.correct: To access detailed account usage information, including the TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS view, the ACCOUNTADMIN role is required. This role provides the necessary privileges for viewing comprehensive account-wide data.

whyOthersWrong.a: This role primarily manages database objects but doesn’t have the necessary permissions to access account-wide metrics.
whyOthersWrong.b: This is a default role with minimal privileges; it cannot access account-level storage metrics.
whyOthersWrong.d: This role focuses on managing security settings rather than accessing storage metrics.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about Snowflake's Resource Monitors? (Choose two.)

options.text: They can only be created by users with the SYSADMIN role.
Resource Monitors can be set at both account and warehouse levels.
They can be used to suspend a warehouse immediately when a limit is exceeded.
The "Economy" scaling policy must be used with all Resource Monitors.

explanation.correct: Resource Monitors can manage credit usage for an entire account or individual warehouses. Resource Monitors have an option to suspend a warehouse immediately, aborting ongoing queries if the credit limit is reached.

whyOthersWrong.a: This is incorrect; only the ACCOUNTADMIN role has the necessary permissions to create Resource Monitors.
whyOthersWrong.d: This is false; the "Economy" scaling policy relates to warehouse auto-scaling, not directly to Resource Monitors.

questions.question: What information can be obtained from the TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS views in Snowflake? (Choose two.)

options.text: Total storage used for Time Travel
Number of This is not available in the TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS views; it pertains to session monitoring rather than storage.active sessions per database
Total credits used by a specific user
Amount of storage consumed by deleted tables

explanation.correct: his view also provides information on storage used by dropped tables, which remain available through time travel and failsafe features. The TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS views include details on storage for active databases, time travel, and failsafe storage.

whyOthersWrong.c: Credits usage relates to warehouse monitoring and is not included in the TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS views.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the "Standard" and "Economy" scaling policies in Snowflake's multi-cluster warehouses?

options.text: The "Standard" policy shuts down clusters faster than the "Economy" policy.
The "Economy" policy adds clusters immediately when queries are queued.
The "Standard" policy prioritizes performance, while the "Economy" policy conserves credits.
The "Economy" policy is only available in the Enterprise Edition.

explanation.correct: The Standard policy favors performance by starting new clusters as soon as needed, while the Economy policy is designed to be more conservative, saving credits even if it may result in slight delays.

whyOthersWrong.a: The opposite is true; the Economy policy takes longer to shut down clusters, requiring more checks.
whyOthersWrong.b: This is incorrect; the Economy policy is more conservative and does not add clusters immediately.
whyOthersWrong.d: This is not true; both policies are available in multiple Snowflake editions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake accounts is true?

options.text: A single Snowflake account can exist across multiple cloud providers.
Multiple accounts under one organization must be in the same region.
Multiple accounts can be managed centrally using an Org Admin role.
An account can be created without specifying a cloud provider.

explanation.correct: Snowflake allows multiple accounts under one organization to be centrally managed using an Org Admin role, providing a centralized view and management of accounts within the organization.

whyOthersWrong.a: A Snowflake account is always tied to a specific cloud provider and region. It cannot span multiple providers simultaneously.
whyOthersWrong.b: Multiple accounts under an organization can exist in different regions, which is a reason for setting up multiple accounts.
whyOthersWrong.d: When creating a Snowflake account, a specific cloud provider and region must be selected.

questions.question: A Snowflake database can contain multiple schemas, and each schema can hold objects such as tables, views, and user-defined functions.

explanation.correct: In Snowflake, a database can contain multiple schemas, and each schema serves as a logical container for various database objects such as tables, views, stages, user-defined functions, and other database components.

whyOthersWrong.b: This is incorrect because Snowflake’s architecture supports organizing objects using databases and schemas as logical containers, allowing multiple schemas within a database.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using the 'USE' command in Snowflake SQL? (Choose two.)

options.text: To set the context for the active database.
To change the current user's role.
To set the schema context for subsequent queries.
To automatically refresh the Snowflake warehouse.

explanation.correct: The 'USE' command can also set the schema context, which means subsequent queries will automatically operate within the chosen schema, making it unnecessary to provide fully qualified table names. The 'USE' command allows setting the active database context so that all subsequent queries operate within that database unless otherwise specified.

whyOthersWrong.b: Changing a user’s role in Snowflake requires the 'SET ROLE' command, not the 'USE' command.
whyOthersWrong.d: The 'USE' command does not refresh or interact with the virtual warehouse.

questions.question: Which Snowflake object can be used to monitor and manage resource usage within an account?

explanation.correct: Resource Monitors in Snowflake are designed to monitor and manage resource usage, such as compute time and storage costs, ensuring the account stays within specified limits.

whyOthersWrong.a: Virtual Warehouses provide compute power for executing queries but do not have the capability to monitor resource usage.
whyOthersWrong.c: The Public Schema is a default schema provided within each database but is not related to resource monitoring.
whyOthersWrong.d: Stages are used for data loading and unloading but do not monitor resources.

questions.question: Which of the following Snowflake commands is used to upload files from a local system to an internal stage?

explanation.correct: The PUT command is used in Snowflake to upload files from a local system to an internal stage. It is the appropriate command when you want to prepare files for loading into a Snowflake table.

whyOthersWrong.a: The COPY INTO command is used to load data from a stage into a table or unload data from a table into a stage, not for uploading files from a local system.
whyOthersWrong.c: The GET command is used to download files from a stage to a local system. It is the reverse of the PUT command.
whyOthersWrong.d: The LIST command is used to list files currently available in a stage; it does not upload files.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of internal stage in Snowflake?

explanation.correct: There is no "Schema stage" in Snowflake. The internal stages in Snowflake include User stages, Table stages, and Named internal stages. These internal stages allow different levels of access and control, but none is associated with a schema directly.

whyOthersWrong.a: The User stage is a valid internal stage tied to individual users.
whyOthersWrong.c: The Named internal stage is a flexible and customizable stage created and managed like any other database object in Snowflake.
whyOthersWrong.d: The Table stage is another valid internal stage specifically associated with an individual table.

questions.question: External stages in Snowflake must always include storage credentials within the stage definition.

explanation.correct: While external stages can include credentials, it is not required or recommended. The preferred method is to use a storage integration object to securely manage credentials separately from the stage definition. This improves security by preventing direct exposure of sensitive information like access keys.

whyOthersWrong.a: If selected, this is incorrect because including storage credentials directly in the stage definition is not necessary. Using a storage integration object is the best practice, allowing for better security and reusability across multiple stages.

questions.question: What is the recommended method for specifying file format properties when using the COPY INTO command?

options.text: Specifying the file format properties directly in each COPY INTO command
Defining the file format properties directly in the stage object
Using a file format object and referencing it in the stage
Snowflake does not support specifying file format properties separately

explanation.correct: The recommended method is to create a separate file format object and reference it in the stage. This allows for consistency and reusability, as the same file format can be applied across multiple stages without redefinition. This approach also keeps configurations organized and easy to manage.

whyOthersWrong.a: While it's possible to specify file format properties directly in each COPY INTO command, it is not recommended as it can lead to redundancy and inconsistency.
whyOthersWrong.b: Defining file format properties directly in the stage is an option, but using a file format object is more flexible and reusable, which is why it is recommended.
whyOthersWrong.d: Snowflake does support specifying file format properties separately, and it is a key feature that allows flexibility in data loading processes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the COPY INTO command in Snowflake?

options.text: The COPY INTO command can only load data from internal stages.
The file format must always be specified directly in the COPY INTO command for it to work.
The COPY INTO command requires an active warehouse for execution.
Unloading data using the COPY INTO command is not possible.

explanation.correct: The COPY INTO command requires an active virtual warehouse to provide the compute resources necessary for loading or unloading data. Without an active warehouse, the command cannot execute as there are no compute resources to process the data.

whyOthersWrong.a: This is incorrect because the COPY INTO command can load data from both internal and external stages, as long as they are properly configured.
whyOthersWrong.b: While the file format can be specified directly in the COPY INTO command, it is not mandatory. The file format can be predefined in a stage or a separate file format object, allowing for flexibility.
whyOthersWrong.d: The COPY INTO command can indeed be used for unloading data from a table to a stage. This is done by specifying the stage as the target and the table as the source in the command.

questions.question: Which command in Snowflake allows you to replace all existing rows in a table with new data?

explanation.correct: The INSERT OVERWRITE command removes all existing rows in a table and replaces them with the new rows specified in the command. It effectively truncates the table before inserting the new data.

whyOthersWrong.a: The UPDATE command modifies existing rows based on conditions but does not replace all rows.
whyOthersWrong.b: The INSERT command adds new rows to the table but does not remove or overwrite existing ones.
whyOthersWrong.d: There is no TRUNCATE AND INSERT command in Snowflake.

questions.question: When using the UPDATE command in Snowflake, omitting the WHERE clause will result in all rows being updated with the specified values.

explanation.correct: If the WHERE clause is omitted in the UPDATE command, Snowflake will apply the update to every row in the table. This is because the absence of a filter means all rows meet the condition by default.

whyOthersWrong.b: This is incorrect because, without a WHERE clause, there is no filtering, and all rows will be affected.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowpipe is false?

options.text: Snowpipe is a serverless feature that does not require a user-created warehouse.
Snowpipe can be paused and resumed using the ALTER PIPE command.
Snowpipe only supports file sizes between 100 MB and 200 MB.
Snowpipe's cost is based on a per-second per-core granularity.

explanation.correct: While Snowpipe recommends files be between 100 MB and 200 MB to optimize performance and cost, it is not limited to only supporting files within this size range. Files smaller or larger can still be processed.

whyOthersWrong.a: This statement is true as Snowpipe uses serverless compute resources managed by Snowflake.
whyOthersWrong.b: Snowpipe can indeed be paused and resumed using the ALTER PIPE command, allowing for flexible management.
whyOthersWrong.d: Snowpipe’s billing is based on a per-second per-core granularity, which accurately reflects the compute resources used.

questions.question: Which of the following is the default value for the ON_ERROR option when using Snowflake’s bulk loading process?

explanation.correct: The default value for the ON_ERROR option in Snowflake's bulk loading process is ABORT_STATEMENT. This setting stops the entire loading process when any error is encountered in any file or row, ensuring that no partial data is loaded.

whyOthersWrong.a: CONTINUE allows the loading to proceed even if errors are encountered, but this is not the default behavior for bulk loading.
whyOthersWrong.b: SKIP_FILE skips files with errors but is not the default value for bulk loading; it is the default for Snowpipe.
whyOthersWrong.d: SKIP_FILE_PERCENTAGE specifies a percentage of errors for which files are skipped, but it is not the default setting.

questions.question: What happens when the PURGE option is set to TRUE in a Snowflake COPY command?

options.text: Files are automatically deleted from the stage after a successful load
Files are validated but not loaded
Files are moved to a backup location after the load

explanation.correct: When the PURGE option is set to TRUE, Snowflake deletes the files from the stage once they have been successfully loaded into the table. This helps in managing storage and preventing duplicate data loads.

whyOthersWrong.a: Compression is not controlled by the PURGE option; this is handled separately.
whyOthersWrong.c: The validation mode option (VALIDATE) controls whether files are checked but not loaded, not the PURGE option.
whyOthersWrong.d: The PURGE option deletes files rather than moving them to a backup location.

questions.question: Which of the following transformations is NOT supported directly in the COPY INTO command in Snowflake?

options.text: Filtering rows using a WHERE clause

explanation.correct: Filtering rows using a WHERE clause is not supported in the COPY INTO command. The command allows some basic transformations such as column reordering, data type casting, and truncating column values, but complex operations like filtering rows are not permitted.

whyOthersWrong.a: Reordering columns is supported in the COPY INTO command through the use of a SELECT statement within the command.
whyOthersWrong.c: Casting data types is allowed and can be done using SQL functions in the COPY INTO command.
whyOthersWrong.d: Truncating column values using the TRUNCATECOLUMNS option is supported for managing column length.

questions.question: Which of the following SQL functions can be used within the COPY INTO command to transform data while loading it into Snowflake? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: TO_DATE is a scalar function supported in the COPY INTO command that allows for casting data types, such as converting strings to date formats. UPPER is also a scalar function that can be used within the COPY INTO command to transform data by converting text to uppercase.

whyOthersWrong.b: GROUP BY is not supported in the COPY INTO command as aggregation operations are not allowed.
whyOthersWrong.d: FLATTEN is used for semi-structured data processing and is not supported directly in the COPY INTO command.

questions.question: Which type of function in Snowflake returns one value per row of input?

explanation.correct: Scalar functions return a single value for each row of input, such as converting text to uppercase (UPPER) or formatting dates (TO_DATE).

whyOthersWrong.b: Aggregate functions return one value for an entire group of rows, such as SUM or MAX.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake’s COPY INTO command is TRUE?

options.text: It supports aggregation functions like SUM and AVG.
It can use a select statement to cast column data types during loading.
It supports using the JOIN clause to combine data from multiple sources.
It allows filtering data with GROUP BY and WHERE clauses.

explanation.correct: The COPY INTO command in Snowflake can use a select statement to cast column data types, which is useful for transforming data during the loading process.

whyOthersWrong.a: Aggregation functions like SUM and AVG are not supported in the COPY INTO command.
whyOthersWrong.c: Joins are not supported within the COPY INTO command as it is designed for straightforward transformations.
whyOthersWrong.d: Filtering with GROUP BY and WHERE clauses is not possible within the COPY INTO command.

questions.question: Which Snowflake function is best suited for approximating the number of distinct values in a large dataset to improve performance over exact calculation?

explanation.correct: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT uses the HyperLogLog algorithm to efficiently estimate the number of distinct values in large datasets, providing a fast alternative to exact calculations.

whyOthersWrong.a: COUNT provides an exact count, which can be compute-intensive for large datasets.
whyOthersWrong.c: DISTINCT identifies unique values but does not optimize performance for large-scale counting.
whyOthersWrong.d: SUM is used for summing numerical values and is not relevant for counting distinct values.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the primary difference between a Stored Procedure and a User Defined Function (UDF) in Snowflake?

options.text: Stored Procedures must always return a value, while UDFs do not.
UDFs are used for performing database operations such as updates and deletes, while Stored Procedures are for calculating and returning values.
Stored Procedures can perform multiple operations without returning a value, while UDFs must return a value and are typically used in queries.
UDFs can execute with either caller’s or owner’s rights, while Stored Procedures do not have this capability.

explanation.correct: Stored Procedures can indeed perform multiple database operations without returning a value, while UDFs are meant to return a value and are typically used within select statements to calculate and return values. This statement accurately distinguishes their use cases.

whyOthersWrong.a: Stored Procedures do not need to return a value. They are designed primarily to perform operations (like inserts, updates, and deletes) and may or may not return a value. UDFs, however, are designed to calculate and return a value, making this statement inaccurate.
whyOthersWrong.b: This statement reverses the roles of UDFs and Stored Procedures. UDFs are used for returning values within queries, not for performing database operations. Stored Procedures are designed to perform such operations.
whyOthersWrong.d: UDFs do not have the capability to execute with either the caller's or owner’s rights; this feature is specific to Stored Procedures, which can be set to run as either the caller or the owner.

questions.question: Which programming languages can be used to create Stored Procedures in Snowflake? (Choose three)

explanation.correct: Python can be used to create Stored Procedures in Snowflake through Snowpark. This allows developers to write procedures in a familiar and versatile programming language. Scala is another supported language for creating Stored Procedures in Snowflake using Snowpark, making it a valid option. JavaScript is commonly used for writing Stored Procedures in Snowflake. It is a standard language choice for procedural logic within Snowflake.

whyOthersWrong.c: Although Snowflake Scripting extends SQL to include procedural logic, it is not the same as using pure SQL as a programming language for Stored Procedures. Instead, Snowflake Scripting acts as an extension of SQL.
whyOthersWrong.e: Ruby is not supported for writing Stored Procedures in Snowflake. Only certain programming languages like Python, Scala, and JavaScript are available.

questions.question: When creating a Stored Procedure in Snowflake, which of the following is true regarding its return type?

options.text: A return type is optional for Stored Procedures.
The return type must always be specified, even if no value is returned.
Stored Procedures in Snowflake can only return integer types.
A return type should only be specified if the procedure returns a value.

explanation.correct: The return type must always be specified in Snowflake, even if the Stored Procedure does not return any value. It is a required part of the procedure's definition.

whyOthersWrong.a: In Snowflake, the return type is mandatory when creating a Stored Procedure, regardless of whether the procedure actually returns a value. Therefore, stating it as optional is not accurate.
whyOthersWrong.c: Stored Procedures in Snowflake are not limited to returning integer types. They can return a variety of data types, making this statement incorrect.
whyOthersWrong.d: The return type must be specified whether the procedure returns a value or not, so this statement is not true. It suggests that return type declaration is conditional, which it is not.

questions.question: What is the default execution context for Stored Procedures in Snowflake if the execution context (caller or owner) is not explicitly specified?

explanation.correct: The default execution context for Stored Procedures is the owner’s rights if nothing is specified. This setting ensures that the procedure executes with the permissions of the procedure’s owner by default.

whyOthersWrong.a: If the execution context is not specified, Stored Procedures in Snowflake default to the owner’s rights. The caller’s rights must be explicitly set using EXECUTE AS CALLER.
whyOthersWrong.c: "Admin" is not a valid execution context option in Snowflake for Stored Procedures. The execution context is limited to either the caller’s or the owner’s rights.
whyOthersWrong.d: "System" is also not a valid execution context in Snowflake. The default and configurable options are strictly limited to either caller or owner.

questions.question: Which of the following Snowflake features allows executing code that is stored and executed outside of Snowflake, often used for integrating third-party services?

explanation.correct: External Functions are designed to integrate Snowflake with external services and execute code outside of Snowflake. They allow users to leverage third-party APIs, external data sources, and additional programming languages beyond what is available internally.

whyOthersWrong.a: Stored Procedures are executed within Snowflake’s environment. They are not designed to execute code stored externally and cannot directly integrate with third-party services in the same manner as External Functions.
whyOthersWrong.b: User Defined Functions (UDFs) are executed within Snowflake itself and are not intended to connect with external environments or services. They process data internally within the Snowflake ecosystem.
whyOthersWrong.d: Secure Functions refer to the secure implementation of UDFs or Stored Procedures within Snowflake to protect sensitive information. They do not relate to executing external code or integrating with outside services.

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to access elements within a variant column in Snowflake?

options.text: Using a semicolon after the column name
Using a dollar sign ($) followed by the number of the column
Using the colon (:) to access elements by name
Using parentheses to specify the element's path

explanation.correct: In Snowflake, to access specific elements within a variant column, the colon (:) is used after the column name. This syntax allows you to access elements within semi-structured data stored in the variant column.

whyOthersWrong.a: A semicolon is not used in accessing elements within a variant column.
whyOthersWrong.b: The dollar sign ($) followed by a number is used for positional access, but not directly for accessing elements by name.
whyOthersWrong.d: Parentheses are not used for accessing elements in variant columns. Instead, they are used in other contexts like function calls.

questions.question: Which Snowflake function is used to convert hierarchical semi-structured data into a relational table view?

explanation.correct: The FLATTEN function in Snowflake is used to convert hierarchical data within semi-structured data types (such as arrays in JSON) into a table view. This allows users to work with nested data in a more structured format.

whyOthersWrong.a: PARSE_JSON is used for interpreting strings as JSON but does not flatten data into a table view.
whyOthersWrong.b: A lateral view is created when FLATTEN is used but is not itself a function.
whyOthersWrong.d: EXPAND_ARRAY is not a valid Snowflake function for working with semi-structured data.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the use of the FLATTEN function in Snowflake is TRUE?

options.text: It can be used within the COPY command for data loading.
It returns a lateral view, which can be joined with the original table.
It only works with JSON strings, not arrays.
It must be used with structured data types.

explanation.correct: The FLATTEN function returns a lateral view in Snowflake, allowing it to be joined with other tables, including the original data source. This is useful for working with nested or hierarchical data structures like arrays.

whyOthersWrong.a: The FLATTEN function cannot be used within the COPY command.
whyOthersWrong.c: FLATTEN works with arrays, not just JSON strings.
whyOthersWrong.d: FLATTEN is designed for semi-structured data, not structured data types.

questions.question: The function PARSE_JSON in Snowflake can be used to insert JSON data directly into a variant column using the INSERT INTO VALUES syntax.

explanation.correct: The PARSE_JSON function is used to interpret strings as JSON documents, but when inserting JSON data into a variant column in Snowflake, the syntax INSERT INTO VALUES does not directly work. Instead, you must use a SELECT statement with PARSE_JSON to insert the interpreted JSON data.

whyOthersWrong.a: This option is incorrect because INSERT INTO VALUES alone does not support direct JSON interpretation without using SELECT and PARSE_JSON.

questions.question: What Snowflake function is used to generate a URL for accessing a file in an external stage with a temporary access period?

explanation.correct: BUILD_SCOPED_FILE_URL is the correct function for generating a temporary, encoded Snowflake-hosted URL to access a file in an external stage. This type of URL has a temporary access period that corresponds to the persisted query result cache period.

whyOthersWrong.a: GET_PRE_SIGNED_URL generates an HTTPS URL for accessing the file directly, but it is not temporary based on cache expiry like the scoped URL.
whyOthersWrong.c: BUILD_STAGE_FILE_URL is used for generating a permanent access URL, not a temporary one.
whyOthersWrong.d: GENERATE_FILE_LINK is not a valid Snowflake function.

questions.question: What is the purpose of enabling the directory table in a Snowflake stage?

options.text: To store user data in the Snowflake stage.
To query metadata of the staged files, including file URLs.
To directly access and modify files in the stage.
To create and manage users within the stage.

explanation.correct: Enabling the directory table allows users to query metadata information (such as file URLs, file sizes, and modification times) of the files stored in a Snowflake stage.

whyOthersWrong.a: The directory table does not store user data; it stores metadata about files staged in Snowflake.
whyOthersWrong.c: Directory tables provide metadata access, but they do not allow direct file modifications.
whyOthersWrong.d: User management is not related to the directory table function.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about enabling a directory table in Snowflake?

options.text: It is enabled by default when creating a stage.
It can only be enabled during the creation of a stage.
It requires a manual refresh of metadata when enabled.
It automatically refreshes the metadata every 5 minutes.

explanation.correct: When a directory table is enabled, the metadata of the files must be refreshed manually using the ALTER STAGE command. Without this refresh, the metadata will not be up-to-date.

whyOthersWrong.a: The directory table is not enabled by default; it must be explicitly enabled.
whyOthersWrong.b: It can be enabled both during creation and by altering an existing stage.
whyOthersWrong.d: Automatic refresh can be set up using event notifications, but it is not enabled by default.

questions.question: Which command is used to refresh metadata in a Snowflake directory table after it is enabled?

explanation.correct: The correct command to refresh the metadata in the directory table is ALTER STAGE <stage_name> REFRESH. This refreshes the metadata so that newly staged files and their properties become visible in the directory table.

whyOthersWrong.a: ALTER TABLE is used for table operations, not for stages or directory tables.
whyOthersWrong.b: REFRESH STAGE is not a valid command in Snowflake.
whyOthersWrong.c: ALTER STAGE REFRESH DIRECTORY is not a correct syntax for refreshing metadata.

questions.question: Which sampling method in Snowflake is more efficient for querying large datasets?

explanation.correct: The system or block method is more efficient for large datasets as it operates at the micro-partition level instead of the individual row level, making it faster and less resource-intensive.

whyOthersWrong.a: The row method applies sampling at the individual row level, which can be slower for large datasets.
whyOthersWrong.c: A full table scan does not involve sampling and is the least efficient for large datasets.
whyOthersWrong.d: Snowflake does not have a "Clustered index method" for sampling.

questions.question: What must be done after enabling a directory table in an existing Snowflake stage to ensure that metadata for files already in the stage is available for queries?

options.text: Alter the stage and set the AUTO REFRESH parameter.
Manually refresh the stage using an ALTER STAGE command.
Wait for 24 hours for the system to sync the metadata.

explanation.correct: Manually refreshing the stage with an ALTER STAGE <stage_name> REFRESH command is necessary to make the metadata for existing files available immediately.

whyOthersWrong.a: Restarting the Snowflake instance is not required or relevant to refreshing metadata.
whyOthersWrong.b: While auto-refresh can be set up using event notifications, it is not sufficient to access existing file metadata without a manual refresh.
whyOthersWrong.d: The system does not automatically sync metadata within a fixed time; a manual refresh is required.

questions.question: Which of the following programming languages can be used with Snowflake connectors or APIs to build applications that connect and perform operations with Snowflake? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Snowflake provides a Python connector that enables developers to build applications and perform various operations in Snowflake using Python. Python is also supported in Snowpark for writing and executing code serverlessly within Snowflake. Snowflake supports Java through the JDBC driver, allowing integration with most client tools and Java-based applications to connect to and perform operations in Snowflake.

whyOthersWrong.b: While C# is a popular programming language, it is not directly supported by Snowflake connectors like JDBC or Python.
whyOthersWrong.d: Ruby is not natively supported by Snowflake connectors or Snowpark, so it cannot be used directly with Snowflake to perform operations.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Snowflake's Partner Connect feature?

options.text: To allow users to connect Snowflake to third-party tools and services with minimal setup
To provide a built-in code editor for developing Snowpark applications
To manage and schedule virtual warehouses automatically
To automate the creation of database schemas based on external data sources

explanation.correct: Partner Connect is a Snowflake feature that simplifies the process of integrating Snowflake with third-party tools and services. It allows users with the ACCOUNTADMIN role to set up trial accounts and connect these tools seamlessly within the Snowflake interface, enhancing integration with external services with just a few clicks.

whyOthersWrong.b: Partner Connect does not provide a code editor for Snowpark applications; this functionality is related to Snowflake worksheets or external development environments.
whyOthersWrong.c: Virtual warehouses are managed independently of Partner Connect, which is designed for external tool integration rather than managing compute resources.
whyOthersWrong.d: While Snowflake allows data loading from external sources, Partner Connect is not specifically designed for automating database schema creation. It focuses on tool and service integration.

questions.question: What feature in Snowflake allows users to access historical versions of their data or recover dropped objects within a specified time period?

explanation.correct: Time Travel is a feature in Snowflake that enables users to access historical data versions and recover dropped objects such as tables, schemas, and databases within a specified retention period.

whyOthersWrong.a: Failsafe is a disaster recovery feature, but it requires intervention from Snowflake support and is used beyond the Time Travel period.
whyOthersWrong.b: Cloning allows creating a snapshot of a database or table, but it doesn't directly relate to accessing past versions.
whyOthersWrong.d: Version Control is not a feature in Snowflake; Snowflake uses Time Travel for versioning data.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake's Failsafe feature is TRUE?

options.text: It can be configured to last up to 90 days.
It requires user action to restore data.
It is only available for permanent tables.
It is available for all table types, including temporary tables.

explanation.correct: Failsafe is only available for permanent tables in Snowflake. It provides an additional seven-day period for recovery beyond the configured Time Travel period.

whyOthersWrong.a: The Failsafe period is fixed at seven days and is not configurable.
whyOthersWrong.b: Users cannot perform actions directly through Failsafe; it requires Snowflake support intervention.
whyOthersWrong.d: Failsafe is not available for temporary or transient tables.

questions.question: If a user drops a table in Snowflake, which feature must they use to recover it, assuming the operation is within the retention period?

explanation.correct: Time Travel is the feature in Snowflake that allows users to restore dropped tables (as well as schemas and databases) as long as the operation occurs within the set retention period.

whyOthersWrong.a: Snapshot Restore is not a feature in Snowflake.
whyOthersWrong.b: Data Cloning creates a copy of the table but doesn't restore a dropped table.
whyOthersWrong.d: Auto-Recovery is not an available feature in Snowflake.

questions.question: How many days can the retention period be set for Time Travel in a Snowflake account with the Enterprise Edition?

explanation.correct: For Snowflake’s Enterprise Edition and above, the Time Travel retention period can be set up to 90 days, giving flexibility in data recovery options.

whyOthersWrong.a: 1 day is the limit for the Standard Edition, not the Enterprise Edition.
